_README: Regression set for retrieval and answer quality. Run after any change to
search-term generation, tier filters, the quality floor, scoring, or the
library/live routing gate.
Every number the project currently quotes about its own behaviour is a
single live observation. This file exists so those become tracked metrics.
Fields per case:
id                 stable slug
question           exactly as a clinician would type it
mode               review | learn
expect.route       library | live   (which retrieval path should win)
expect.min_papers  floor on evidence-base size
expect.min_sr      minimum Cochrane + Level I papers
expect.min_rct     minimum Level I papers
expect.modules_non_empty   learn mode: every module must be generated
expect.max_unsourced_numeric_modules  modules with numeric params and 0 citations
why                what this case is guarding against
TO FILL IN: cases 2-20. Half should be topics the library covers well
(expect route=library) and half genuinely thin (expect route=live). That
split is a clinical judgement call — it needs RB, not the model, or the
baseline measures assumptions rather than reality.

cases.question: Use of lasers in root canal disinfection
why: Retrieval regression, 2026-08-29. esearch returned 5 PMIDs across 28
queries because module search strings were bags of words that PubMed
ANDs together ('laser irradiation power settings endodontic
disinfection' matches 1 record in all of PubMed). Module 4 retrieved
zero papers and still emitted a numeric protocol - Er:YAG 20 mJ/15 Hz,
5.25% NaOCl 2 mL/60 s, ISO #30/.04 - invented and shipped behind a
disclaimer.
This topic is also a vocabulary trap: the literature lives under aPDT,
PIPS, SWEEPS, photodynamic therapy and Er:YAG, so any query that does
not OR-expand synonyms will miss it while appearing to succeed.
The first post-fix run reported 10 Cochrane reviews, which is not a
plausible number for this topic and was not real. COCHRANE_TERM was
'Cochrane Review[pt]', a publication type PubMed does not have; it was
translated to a word match on 'cochrane' ANDed with Review[pt], so any
SR that mentioned searching the Cochrane Library was promoted to the
top tier. Fixed to a journal-scoped filter. 109 library rows carrying
the false tag were demoted and rescored (median -7.8).
route is 'any' deliberately. The first fixed run went live and wrote
196 papers back into the library, so the same question now serves from
the library. That is the learning loop working as designed; pinning
the route would make a correct behaviour look like a regression.

baseline.note: Library route, measured by scripts/probe_retrieval.py after the Cochrane tier fix.

superseded_baseline.note: First post-fix run, live route. Its Cochrane count was inflated by the fake publication-type filter; kept because the paper count and module numbers were real.

regression_reference.note: The failing run, kept so the diff stays legible.
